Ludi Harpastum (also: Harpastum Festival, Games Harpastum): Ludi Harpastum is one of Mondstadt's oldest festivals, held every year and lasting fifteen days. It is a carnival of songs, wine and flight, the very things Mondstadt takes pride in, and it is especially loved by children. The champion of the games chooses a maiden who, at the climax, throws the Harpastum, a round ball wrapped in red cloth, into the crowd. Whoever catches it is said to enjoy a year of fortune and happiness.

Practice: Fifteen days of games, music, food and drink. At the climax a maiden chosen by the champion throws the red-cloth Harpastum ball to the crowd; the person who picks it up is blessed with a year of fortune.

History: Founded to mark Barbatos teaching his people to brew wine and live freely. About a thousand years before the main story the aristocracy that ruled Mondstadt turned it into an elite affair, until Vennessa's rebellion restored it.

Scene use: Use it for crowded, joyful scenes in Mondstadt: music in the streets, wine and food stalls, children running about, a gliding contest or the red Harpastum ball thrown to the crowd.

1.content:
Bards and Music of Mondstadt (also: Mondstadt bards, Bards of Mondstadt, Bardic tradition of Mondstadt): Mondstadt is known as a land of poetry, song and wine, and bards are woven into daily life: they play in the plaza, in taverns and at festivals, and they are paid in Mora or in drinks. The tradition is tied to freedom. In the days of the tyrant Decarabian, songs of resistance were sung in cellars and alleys, and a young bard of Old Mondstadt played his lyre in the rebellion. Barbatos, the Anemo Archon, later took that bard's name and appearance and still wanders the city as the bard Venti.

Practice: Bards perform on the streets, in squares and in taverns, often for tips or drinks. Inspired travelling bards come to Mondstadt, especially around Ludi Harpastum, and sing poems in the streets.

Songs and lore: Songs carry Mondstadt's story. A song of resistance was whispered in dark places under Decarabian and later under the corrupt nobility, and became an anthem for the rebels.

Scene use: Use a bard as colour: a lyre in a tavern, a song in the plaza, a poem sold for a drink. Songs in Mondstadt are about wind, wine, freedom and its history.

2.content: Mondstadt Cuisine (also: Mondstadt food, Mondstadter cuisine, Mondstadt dishes, Mondstadt cooking): Mondstadt cooking is simple, hearty country food shaped by the nation's two great loves, wine and song. Apples, potatoes, cheese, butter, milk and cream turn up everywhere. Signature dishes include Mondstadt Hash Browns eaten with jam, peppered Mondstadt Grilled Fish, the festival meat pie called Moon Pie, honey-roasted Sweet Madame and the steak-and-cheese stack "Pile 'Em Up". The famous drink is dandelion wine, followed by apple cider, alcoholic or not. Drinking is a big part of social life, at taverns such as Angel's Share and the Cat's Tail, and the popular restaurant is Good Hunter.

3.content:
Daily Life in Mondstadt (also: Mondstadt customs, Mondstadter way of life, Life in Mondstadt): Mondstadt is a laid-back city-state of farms, windmills, vineyards and taverns where freedom, wine and song are the shared ideals. No monarch rules it. The Knights of Favonius keep order, the Church of Favonius handles worship, and the Adventurers' Guild takes on odd jobs. Ordinary life is peaceful, social and open to outsiders.

Practice: - **Work.** Farming, winemaking, hunting, smithing, trading and serving in taverns are the usual trades. Apples, grapes and sunsettias are plentiful, and most farms have a windmill.
- **Drink.** Dandelion wine and apple cider are the best-known drinks. Alcohol is part of social life, from the Angel's Share tavern to family dinners.
- **Order.** The Knights patrol the city and countryside, settle disputes and fight hilichurls. Most people expect help from them rather than fear them.

Scene use: Set scenes in a warm, breezy city: windmills turning, wine and apples at stalls, bards in the plaza, Knights in white armour on patrol and gliders overhead. Mondstadters are friendly, informal and curious about travellers.

4.content:
Mondstadt Fashion (also: Mondstadt clothing, Mondstadt attire, Mondstadt uniforms): Mondstadt dress is practical folk clothing. Men wear wide trousers tucked into tall boots, women wear dirndl-style dresses or blouses with bodices, and children dress as small versions of the adults. Distinct uniforms mark bards (green), maids, Church of Favonius sisters (black habits, rarely white) and the Knights of Favonius (black clothing under white plate armour with wing motifs).

Practice: - Boys: short-sleeved tunics with short vests and short trousers.
- Men: wide trousers tucked into tall boots; several shirt and vest variants exist, including a distinct style for elderly men.
- Girls and women: dirndl-style dresses, often pink or blue for girls and red, orange or blue for women; other women's outfits use detached sleeves, bloomers and short boots.

Scene use: Describe townsfolk in vests, boots and dirndls, knights in white armour with wing motifs, bards in green and sisters in black habits when you need Mondstadt to feel recognisable at a glance.

5.content:
Religion in Mondstadt (also: Mondstadt faith, worship of the Anemo Archon, Barbatos worship, Mondstadt Cathedral worship): Mondstadt worships Barbatos, the Anemo Archon and God of Freedom. Devotion runs through the Church of Favonius and its Cathedral in Mondstadt City, the Statues of the Seven, a few ancient ruined temples and festivals such as Windblume, Ludi Harpastum and Weinlesefest. The faith is relaxed: Barbatos asked for freedom rather than obedience, so people honour him with wine, song and flowers more than strict doctrine. Most worshippers do not know that their god walks the streets as the bard Venti.

Practice: - Prayer and blessing. Sisters pray at the Cathedral; Seamus Pegg greets people with May the Anemo Archon protect you on your path. Rosaria, the irreverent nun, skips prayers.
- Offerings. People with Visions offer Anemoculi at Statues of the Seven; festivals offer flowers (Windblume), wine (Ludi Harpastum, Weinlesefest).

Scene use: Keep the faith as gentle background, warm and informal. Do not have Mondstadters preach doctrine or recognise Venti as a god.

key: Festival of the Returning Wind and Fine Wine
6.content:
Weinlesefest (also: Wine Harvest Festival, Festival of the Returning Wind and Fine Wine): Weinlesefest ("wine harvest festival" in German) is held in Mondstadt every autumn, when the west wind returns with the harvest. Citizens brew fresh wine and keep it sealed until Windcoming Day, when it is uncasked to invite the Anemo Archon to share a drink. If the Archon is pleased with the wine, a gentle breeze is summoned to bless the people.

Practice: New wine is brewed and sealed during the harvest season, then opened on Windcoming Day in a toast to the Anemo Archon. A breeze afterwards is read as his blessing.

Scene use: Use it for warm autumn scenes: stalls at Springvale, barrels, fruit carts, a stage with music and the question of whether the wind will come. It suits quiet talks over wine and family reminiscence.

7.content:
Windblume Festival (also: Windblume): The Windblume Festival is Mondstadt's once-yearly festival of love and freedom, and Klee calls it the city's biggest celebration. The city is decorated, and people offer Windblumes to the Anemo Archon Barbatos and to anyone they love or admire. Gifts and love poems can go with them, but the flowers are not only romantic. People also use the festival to mend or deepen any relationship. "Windblume" (German for "wind flower") began as a secret code word among the rebels against the tyrant god Decarabian. Today nobody agrees which flower the Windblume really is.

Practice: People offer Windblumes informally at the great statue of Barbatos all through the festival, and give flowers to loved ones. Florists such as Flora have more customers than they can handle.

Origins: In Old Mondstadt, Decarabian ruled from his tower. People who planned to overthrow him used "Windblume" as their secret sign. The festival grew out of that rebellion; when it was first held is unknown.

Scene use: Use it for light-hearted Mondstadt scenes: decorated streets, flower stalls, music, wine, couples at Cape Oath, people working up courage to give someone flowers. Shopkeepers and the Guild may turn down offers of help, saying people do things themselves at Windblume.
